course_name_original: HIDRAULICA APLICADA A PROYECTOS DE DESARROLLO

learning_outcomes.text: Applied knowledge of the fundamentals of fluid-mechanical systems and machines.
Know and apply knowledge of basic sciences and technologies to engineering practice.

Possess the ability to design, develop, implement, manage, and improve products, systems, and processes in various industrial fields, using appropriate analytical, computational, or experimental techniques.
Apply acquired knowledge to identify, formulate, and solve problems in broad contexts, being able to integrate them by working in multidisciplinary teams.
Understand the impact of engineering on the environment, the sustainable development of society, and the importance of working in a professional and responsible environment.
Incorporate ICT and industrial engineering technologies and tools into professional activities.
Training in the field of hydraulic technology appropriate for human development, training in its design and practical use.
Knowledge of field experiences in all aspects and phases of projects based on hydraulic applications.
Approach to the reality of the South and cooperation as a way of professional fulfillment in engineering.
Introduction to the multidirectional scope of technology-based development projects.

syllabus_topics: DESIGN AND TECHNOLOGY FOR HUMAN DEVELOPMENT
Design and technology for human development.
Objectives and types of technology-based development projects (water, energy, food).
Phases of a technology-based development project.
Evaluation of a project in the field of development cooperation.
Typology of water supply system facilities.
Study and design of supply facilities.
Study of main elements. Intakes, impulsion lines, reservoirs, networks, water points, etc.
Supply using manual, ram, and aerobombs.
Measurement of flow rates and manometric head.
Systems for drinking water and sanitation. Extensive and intensive.
The basic laboratory for water quality control.
Other hydraulic and civil engineering infrastructures.
ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE APPLIED TO DEVELOPMENT COOPERATION
DEVELOPMENT OF WATER AND SANITATION PROJECTS FOR DEVELOPMENT

assessment_methods.method: Report on AI as a tool in hydraulics for development (Memoria IA)
Laboratory work presentation (Presentación trabajo de laboratorio)

assessment_rules: The course uses continuous assessment based on two portfolios, an AI report, and laboratory work. Portfolio I requires attendance at a minimum of 80% of lectures, while Portfolio II requires attendance at all external talks. The grade obtained in the laboratory is preserved for subsequent years, but students may retake it to improve the score, in which case the previous grade is lost. Portfolio II has a minimum passing grade of 5 out of 10. For the extraordinary examination call, assessment is based on a 100% final written exam.
